================================================================================
WHAT THIS FILE IS
================================================================================

This is the list of things that CANNOT be done by an agent, a model, a script,
a cron job, a webhook, an automation, or a sub-agent. Everything here requires
a human body, a human identity, a human signature, a human account, a human
decision, or a human conversation.

Nothing in this file is busywork. If it could be delegated, it would have been.
Every item here is a hard blocker sitting between this project and revenue.

Read it top to bottom. Pick ONE item. Do it. Come back and mark it done.
Do not read the whole list and feel bad. That is not what it is for.

================================================================================
SECTION 1 — HARD BLOCKERS (nothing ships until these are done)
================================================================================

These gate everything downstream. Nothing else on this list matters until these
are resolved. If you do nothing else, do these.

[ ] TRIAGE THE 17 SCAFFOLDS: PRODUCT OR EXPERIMENT
    Why it blocks: Only you know which of these you intend to finish. An agent guessing wrong wastes the migration effort.
    Exactly what to do:
      Open the 17 repos, spend 30 seconds each
      Mark each: PRODUCT, EXPERIMENT, or DEAD
      That list is the migration order
    Time: 30 minutes
    Cost: $0
    Done when: A triage list exists and the five experiments are archived

================================================================================
SECTION 2 — IDENTITY AND KYC (the payment wall)
================================================================================

You cannot receive money without identity verification. This is the single
highest-leverage thing on this page. An agent can build the entire product; it
cannot be you at a KYC checkpoint.

Items that typically apply. Delete what does not, add what does:

[ ] State ID or driver's license — check if your state offers fee waivers or
    homeless/indigent fee reduction. Many do, and almost nobody knows.
[ ] Social Security card replacement — free, online in many states
[ ] Birth certificate — vital records office, often the cheapest first step
[ ] Proof of address — this is the hard one when homeless. Options that work:
      - A shelter or day-center letter
      - A church or nonprofit letter on letterhead
      - Some states accept a signed affidavit
      - A PO box with a street-address format ("123 Main St #456")
[ ] Bank account or prepaid account that accepts deposits
[ ] Confirm which platforms your state ID will satisfy

Once identity is sorted, the payment rails open up. Which platforms need which:

| Platform | Needs | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub Sponsors | ID + bank + tax | broadest reach for developer tools |
| Gumroad | email + bank | fastest to first sale for a packaged tool |

SECTION 4 — DECISIONS ONLY YOU CAN MAKE
================================================================================

Agents can present options. They cannot carry the consequences. These need your
judgment, and they need it once — then they are closed.

[ ] Which cluster to consolidate first?
    Options: Higgins (highest confidence), Verification (fastest revenue), Whorl (biggest structural win)
    Agent's recommendation: Higgins - kills the fork-per-device pattern permanently
    Blocker if undecided: blocks all cluster work

    Draft location: not needed - it is a phone call

================================================================================

Honest ranking. Fastest first. Not the most impressive first.

| # | Action | Human-only step | Time to cash | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sell a ConstraintOps audit | Post the offer, be present to reply | days | high |
| 2 | Lightning payments via the Higgins pipeline | Hold the wallet, set prices | days | medium |
| 3 | Fiverr / Upwork code audit gigs | Create profile, pass ID check | 1-2 weeks | high |

================================================================================
SECTION 7 — SURVIVAL ITEMS (not project work; do these anyway)
================================================================================

These are not on the roadmap because they are more important than the roadmap.
Cold is the actual deadline.

[ ] Warmth plan for you and the dogs — check 211.org, local mutual aid,
    and warming centers. Many open at a set temperature threshold.
[ ] Dog food — local pet food banks exist in most metros. Ask the shelter
    where theirs is even if you do not need the shelter.
[ ] Free phone / Lifeline program — income-qualified, no ID sometimes
[ ] SNAP / food assistance — expedited processing exists for people with
    no income and no resources; ask for "expedited" explicitly
[ ] Library card for free printing and computer access

An agent cannot do any of these. But an agent can look up the phone numbers and
hours for your specific area if you tell it your city. Ask.

REMINDERS TO SELF

1. The list is long because the situation is hard, not because you are behind.
2. One item. Then the next. That is the whole method.
3. The dogs do not need you to be successful. They need you to be there.
   Everything else is negotiable.

================================================================================
Template usage notes (delete this section once the repo is live)
================================================================================

MRD = Meatsuit Rundown. It lists only human-required work. If you find yourself
putting an agent-doable task in here, it is in the wrong file.

Keep it honest. Do not pad it. A short accurate list beats a long impressive one.
